code-card.name: code-card
code-card.doc: Dark editor card. Lines type in spoken chunks or at a steady speed; highlights, active-line bar, Run press. Registers `id` so notes can point at its lines.

params.title: tab title (default main.py)
params.lang: python | c | cpp | java | javascript (default: from the title's extension)
params.recorded: reference mode: the lines exactly as typed in the recording, when `lines` corrects them (rule E9)
params.logic_fix: why a correction changes the output (goes to 'to confirm')
params.fs: font px (default: the kit's code size, 52, fitted to the box; never below 40)
params.type: [{line, at, cps} | {line, parts: [[lastCharIndex, at], ...]}] (parts: each segment on its word, 45 ms/char + 40 ms, max 0.55 s)
params.run: time the Run button is pressed
params.focus: [{keep: [lines], at, until}] dim the other lines

note.name: note
note.doc: An explanation card outside the code, joined to its target by a wire (rule L6). Target a code line, a terminal line, a recording highlight or a point.

params.target: {code: id, line} | {code: id, run: true} | {term: id, line} | {rec: id, hl: name} | {point: [x, y]}
params.elbow_x: ignored: the wire is routed around the other graphics automatically

terminal.name: terminal
terminal.doc: Output panel. With `exec` it runs the code card's program and prints its exact output (input echoed where it is read, errors in red), scrolling like a real terminal. Registers `id` for notes.

params.title: default Output
params.exec: {code: code-card id, stdin: [lines typed into the program], at, pace, times: [t per line], after_input, tone, tones: {line index: tone}, expect_error} runs the code at build time and prints its real output (rule E7)
params.lines: [{text, input, at, tone: ok|warn|bad|dim}] (filled by exec; by hand needs `manual`)
params.manual: reason the output is written by hand (rule E7)
params.lh: line height (default: 1.45 x the kit's terminal size)

tiles.name: tiles
tiles.doc: A row or grid of value tiles that change state (now / ok / bad / skip / dim), e.g. loop values or rounds.

params.label: optional label above (markdown)
params.appear: [t per tile]: each tile enters on the word that names it (rule S2; default: all at `at`)
params.states: [{i: index | value: v, state, at}]: now | ok | bad | skip | dim | on (back to plain) | focus (amber outline; the focus moves: the last focused tile goes back), e.g. a focus each time she names a value (rule S3) | pick (solid blue: the one chosen, e.g. the index asked for)
params.note: {text, at, until} small text under the tiles

trace.name: trace
trace.doc: Loop trace panel: the variable box, the condition check with its True/False result, per iteration. Optionally drives a code card's highlights, a tiles row and a terminal.

params.cond: condition text after the value, e.g. '== 6'
params.iterations: [{v, val: time value appears, chk: time check starts, res: time result shows, result: true|false, pr: time print runs, out: time output appears, out_text}]
params.hit_line: line that runs when true (e.g. break)

problem.name: problem
problem.doc: Problem statement card; phrases colour as they are read out.

variables.name: variables
variables.doc: Variable boxes that update as the code runs (name = value).

params.label: card label (default Variables), e.g. Accessing values

recording-window.name: recording-window
recording-window.doc: The whole screen recording in a branded window, never cropped or zoomed (rule L7); step tracker in the title bar; highlight boxes in recording coordinates. Registers `id` for notes. Needs a recording listed in the spec's recordings.

params.title: window title
params.box: x, y, w[, h] (fits inside; aspect kept)
params.highlights: [{name, box: [x, y, w, h] in recording pixels, at, until}]
params.hide: [{at, until}] periods to hide the window (e.g. concept scenes)

char-scan.name: char-scan
char-scan.doc: A string split into character cells; a pointer walks along and stamps ✓ or ✗ for a test (Python's isalpha, isdigit, isalnum, isupper, islower, isspace); the result pops as True / False.

params.test: alpha | digit | alnum | upper | lower | space
params.marks: optional marks per character instead of a test: ✓ ✗ –
params.label: caption above, e.g. `"Hi5".isalpha()`
params.stop_on_fail: stop at the first ✗, as Python does (default false: check every character)
params.indexes: show indexes under the cells (default false)

term-reveal.name: term-reveal
term-reveal.doc: The key term or a takeaway built word by word (12 words at most). Words in *stars* get the brand gradient.

params.times: optional [time per word]; default staggered from at

rule-stack.name: rule-stack
rule-stack.doc: Two or three short lines that stack into a rule or takeaway; the last line is emphasised.

contrast.name: contrast
contrast.doc: 'X vs Y' split: two titles with a short line each and a 'vs' between.

blocks.name: blocks
blocks.doc: Labelled blocks with icons and arrows on a light blueprint grid (architecture, client-server, request flow). Coordinates relative to the box.

params.nodes: [{id, x, y, w, h, text, icon, at}]
params.grid: true to draw the blueprint grid (default true)

table.name: table
table.doc: A data table (database rows, comparisons). Rows enter when said; cells or rows can be highlighted.

bars.name: bars
bars.doc: Bar chart that builds as values are said.

counter.name: counter
counter.doc: A number that counts up to its value, with a label.

curve.name: curve
curve.doc: Line chart that draws itself (growth, Big-O). Points are in data units.

bug.name: bug
bug.doc: Brand logo, top right, straight on the backdrop (no box); the on-dark version during dark scenes. Stays until the clip ends.

progress.name: progress
progress.doc: Lesson progress: a thin bar across the very top that fills with the lesson's time. Off by default; prompt `Progress bar: on` adds it to every clip.

params.total: the lesson's duration in s (set automatically)

chapter.name: chapter
chapter.doc: Chapter pill, top left: number badge, chapter name · lesson name. Added automatically for every section with `chapter:` (setting chrome.chapters); slides to the next chapter when it changes.

params.name: chapter name (short)
params.prev: {n, name}: the chapter shown before; the pill swaps at `at`

header.name: header
header.doc: Section label and title, top left (the header band).

title-hero.name: title-hero
title-hero.doc: Opening or question title: a label and ONE line of hero text (shrunk to fit its box, never wrapped), optional focus chip.

params.title: one line; *word* = marker highlight, **word** = brand gradient (an old "a\nb" title joins, with b in the gradient)

name-card.name: name-card
name-card.doc: Instructor name card. Only when the instructor introduces themself (rule E5).

agenda.name: agenda
agenda.doc: Numbered list of roomy cards, each entering when said (agenda, plan, steps); the one she is naming is outlined in blue (Rani's agenda).

params.label: optional label above
params.icons: true to show each item's icon on the right

definition.name: definition
definition.doc: One-sentence definition in a card; phrases underline as they are said.

type-cards.name: type-cards
type-cards.doc: 2-4 concept cards side by side (e.g. break / continue / pass).

chips.name: chips
chips.doc: A row of short keyword or question chips.

card.name: card
card.doc: A single text card with an optional icon and label: a takeaway, a fact, a question.

summary.name: summary
summary.doc: Recap rows with optional keyword chips at the end of a row.

params.rows: [{icon, tone, text, at, chips: [{text, tone, at}]}]

flowchart.name: flowchart
flowchart.doc: Nodes and arrows, with an optional marker that walks the path. Node coordinates are relative to the box.

params.nodes: [{id, x, y, w, h, text, kind: box|term|dec|ok, at}]
params.edges: [{from, to, label, tone: hot|green|red, at, path: optional svg path in box coords}]

cutaway.name: cutaway
cutaway.doc: Only when the prompt asks (rule L11: the background stays the brand plate). Full-frame backdrop for a short full-screen moment (rule L3: at most 12 s each, 10% of runtime). Put the scenes that belong to it after it, with box set inside the full frame.

freeform.name: freeform
freeform.doc: Free composition for a moment no template shows well: your own markup (the kit's classes and --fz-* colours, sizes from the type scale) and its animation steps, each on her word. Checked like any scene (sync, sizes, overlaps).

params.html: markup inside the box; give parts classes or ids to animate (start hidden ones with class `hide`)
params.steps: [{sel: CSS selector inside, at, from: {y, x, scale, opacity…} (enter from), to: {…} (change to), dur, ease, out: time, sfx: kind}]

sound.name: sound
sound.doc: One of the editors' sounds on her word, with nothing on screen, for moments no template covers: boing on a playful 'no', ticks while she counts, chime on the final answer, decision when she picks one option. Use rarely.

params.kind: pop | blip | click | decision | tick | ticks | stop | whoosh | page | bad | good | chime | type | boing

studio-tag.name: studio-tag
studio-tag.doc: Light graphic for the instructor's studio shots (rule L4): a keyword, the step in progress or a short takeaway, in the studio frame's free area. 12 words at most.

captions.name: captions
captions.doc: Subtitles. Only when the video prompt switches them on (rule E3).

image.name: image
image.doc: Place an image file from the video's assets (e.g. a screenshot or diagram).

data-flow.name: data-flow
data-flow.doc: Items (chips with icons) fly into a container (database, table, folder, server, cloud) as they are named; the container fills and counts. For collecting / storing / saving data.

params.target: {kind: database|table|folder|server|cloud, label, x, y, size} (box coords; default right side)
params.items: [{text, icon, at, x, y}] flying in at `at` (sources default to a column on the left)
params.count: {to, label} the container counts up as items arrive (optional)

process-flow.name: process-flow
process-flow.doc: Inputs box -> process (spinning icon) -> output card: dots travel through when the process runs. For data -> information, raw -> processed, input -> output.

type-convert.name: type-convert
type-convert.doc: A value changes type: a quoted value with its type badge goes through the conversion function and comes out converted. For input() -> int(), str(), float().

range-gen.name: range-gen
range-gen.doc: A range generator emits its numbers one by one into slots (first ones paced, the rest quickly), optionally stopping at a break value. For range(), loops generating values.

params.max_slots: slots shown (default 10; longer ranges show … and the last)

request-flow.name: request-flow
request-flow.doc: Nodes with big icons; packets travel along curved links when they are sent (request -> processing -> result back). Optional blocked direct path. For client/server, user -> DBMS -> database, API calls.

params.nodes: [{id, text, icon, x, y, at}] (box coords)
params.packets: [{from, to, label, at, dur, kind: req|res}]
params.blocked: {from, to, label, at} dashed red arc with a cross
params.results: [{text, at, x, y}] small cards that appear (e.g. the returned record)

icon-grid.name: icon-grid
icon-grid.doc: A grid of icons standing for many items (students, records, files) with a count; optional magnifier scanning row by row, a found cell, or a cross. For 'thousands of records', manual search.

calendar.name: calendar
calendar.doc: A month calendar (Rani's 'Imagine a calendar'): the card comes in, the dates fill in row by row, one date turns solid blue; optional rows beside it (DAY / MONTH / YEAR) pop in on her words, their values come in as she says them, and an amber outline follows her. For dates, schedules, 'imagine a calendar'.

params.fill_at: when the dates fill in (default at + 0.4)
params.select: {day, at}: that date turns solid blue
params.fields: [{label, value, at, label_at}] rows beside the calendar (label colours: blue, green, amber)
params.focus: [{field: 1-based, at}] the amber outline on a row

form-card.name: form-card
form-card.doc: A record / form / receipt card whose field values type in as they are said. For 'your name, age, branch…', a student record, a filled form.

params.fields: [{label, value, at, label_at}]: label_at = when she names the field (the row pops in then; default with the card), at = when the value types in
params.focus: [{field: 1-based number or label, at}]: the field she is talking about gets the amber outline; it moves with her (rule S3)

db-tables.name: db-tables
db-tables.doc: A database frame with its tables appearing inside, each with rows. For 'a database stores students, faculty, library records…'.

hub.name: hub
hub.doc: A central badge (the system) with spokes to what it does, each appearing as named. For DBMS -> create/retrieve/update/delete, a component and its jobs.

mockup.name: mockup
mockup.doc: A browser window or phone with app screens that change as they are described: typing into fields, pressing buttons, a loading spinner, results. For 'open the portal, log in, click results…', an app.

params.screens: [{at, elements: [{title} | {subtitle} | {field, value, at} | {button, press_at} | {row, value} | {spinner, at, until} | {stat, value} | {badge}]}]
params.cursor: [{x, y, at, click}] in frame coords
params.box: x, y, w, h (default main slot)

callouts.name: callouts
callouts.doc: Short chips that pop up at free positions as each point is said, with a gentle float (pain points, benefits, reactions). Screen coordinates.

params.items: [{text, icon, tone: red|amber|green|'', x, y, at, until}]

checklist.name: checklist
checklist.doc: Rows that tick off one by one as they are said (benefits, requirements, a recap). The last row may be a highlighted conclusion.

params.conclusion: {text, at} dark banner under the list

big-word.name: big-word
big-word.doc: One giant word letter by letter (the term being introduced: DBMS, DATABASE), with an optional expansion line. Once per term, when it is first named.

scene.name: scene
scene.doc: Only when the prompt asks (rule L11: the background stays the brand plate). Compose mode: switch the background behind the instructor to a dark brand scene; text turns light for its duration.

venn.name: venn
venn.doc: Two sets as circles that draw on; each value pops into its region as it is said; an operation fills its region (union, intersection, difference, symmetric difference) in the brand blue; amber rings point at values, red strikes skip them; an optional result row.

params.op: {kind: union | intersection | a-b | b-a | symmetric, at, label}
params.result: {text, at}: a mono row under the circles, e.g. result = {10, 20}

presenter.name: presenter
presenter.doc: Keyed instructor with poses: studio (her whole studio shot, laptop and desk, life-size and centred: the intro), wide, close, side-right, side-left, corner (bottom right, boxed). Added automatically in compose mode from the spec's `presenter.poses`.

params.crop: [x, y, w, h] of the cut-out in source pixels (set by ingest)
params.box: {w, h, margin, radius}: the bottom-right pose sits in a rounded box (setting presenter.corner_box)
params.studio: [{t0, t1, el, crop}]: the keyed studio shots this clip shows (set by build)

corner-box.name: corner-box
corner-box.doc: Rough cuts: frame the instructor's bottom-right area in the brand box during corner shots (added automatically by build).

prop.name: prop
prop.doc: Place a character or prop from the library; optional idle motion and reactions.

picture.name: picture
picture.doc: A picture moment (rule P1): an illustration from the library (kind illustration, or any prop/character) on the word that names the analogy or example, with an optional caption bubble under it, like the manual edit's water-bottle and calendar pictures. One at a time, only at key points.

params.box: x, y, w, h of the picture
params.caption: {text, at} a short line in a soft bubble under the picture (markdown, 12 words max)

prop-move.name: prop-move
prop-move.doc: Move a prop along a path (a car driving past, a ball rolling), with easing and optional speed lines.

params.box: start x, y and size w, h

prop-scene.name: prop-scene
prop-scene.doc: A small staged scene: a ground line (road or desk) with several props, each with its own entrance and moves.

params.box: scene area x, y, w, h (ground sits at the bottom)
params.props: [{asset, x, y, w, h (relative to box), at, flip, moves: [{to: [x, y], at}], react: [{kind, at}]}]

hf.name: hf
hf.doc: Mount an installed HyperFrames registry item (fzv registry list) in a box: its variables set the content, `cues` (word anchors) time its steps.

params.cues: [times] for items with a `cues` variable (one per step)
params.css: {--custom-prop: value} the item's own CSS variables (e.g. text sizes of a component in a small box)

db3d.name: db3d
db3d.doc: 3D: records (labelled cards) fly one by one into a database cylinder that turns slowly; it pulses as each lands and a count rises. For collecting / storing data in a database. One hero moment per video.

params.items: [{text, at}] each card flies in at `at`
params.label: label under the database (default Database)
params.count: {to, label} count shown under the database (optional)
params.box: x, y, w, h (default main slot)

network3d.name: network3d
network3d.doc: 3D: devices on a floor (person, laptop/client, server, database) joined by arcs; request and response packets travel along them on their words. For client/server, user -> DBMS -> database, APIs. One hero moment per video.

params.nodes: [{id, kind: person|laptop|server|database, text, x, z, at}] x -5..5, z -3..3 (floor units)
params.links: [{from, to, at}] arcs draw on at `at`
params.packets: [{from, to, label, at, dur, kind: req|res}]
params.box: x, y, w, h (default main slot)

loop3d.name: loop3d
loop3d.doc: 3D: loop values ride a conveyor one per iteration through a gate that checks the condition; passing values drop into an output tray, the break value turns the gate red and the belt stops. For for-loops, range(), break.

params.times: [time per value] when each value reaches the gate
params.cond: condition label on the gate, e.g. 'i == 6'
params.stop_value: value where break stops the loop (optional)
params.label: caption above the belt (markdown)
params.box: x, y, w, h (default main slot)

sketch-board.name: sketch-board
sketch-board.doc: A clean whiteboard panel for a sketch scene (inside the free area, or full frame inside a cutaway).

sketch-draw.name: sketch-draw
sketch-draw.doc: Draw a library prop or character as marker outlines, stroke by stroke; optional light colour fill afterwards and a handwritten label.

params.fill: true to tint fills after drawing
params.label: {text, at}

sketch-text.name: sketch-text
sketch-text.doc: Handwritten text that writes itself on (left-to-right wipe).

sketch-list.name: sketch-list
sketch-list.doc: Hand-lettered list; each item writes on with a drawn tick or bullet when said.

sketch-flow.name: sketch-flow
sketch-flow.doc: Hand-drawn boxes and arrows (coordinates relative to the box); each part draws on when said.

params.nodes: [{id, x, y, w, h, text, at, tone}]

sketch-mark.name: sketch-mark
sketch-mark.doc: A hand-drawn annotation over anything on screen: circle, underline, arrow, box, tick or cross.

params.shape: circle | underline | arrow | box | tick | cross
params.box: x, y, w, h (for arrow: from top-left to bottom-right)
